title: Reporting Requests with Will, Would and Could — Quiz 137
content:
## Reporting Requests with Will, Would and Could

Recognise a polite request rather than a question about willingness.

### Lesson focus

1. She said to me, “Would you come a little later?”
2. The teacher said to Tom, “Will you be quiet?”

### Understand the pattern

Will, would and could often make requests polite. The intended action can therefore be reported with asked + listener + to-infinitive, rather than as a literal question about ability or willingness.

### Worked answers and explanation

She asked me to come a little later. The teacher asked Tom to be quiet. The second sentence uses asked rather than automatically assuming the teacher was angry. A firmer context could justify told Tom to be quiet.

### Try another

Report the request: Ravi said to me, 'Could you open the door?'

### Suggested answer

Ravi asked me to open the door. This captures the request. 'Ravi asked whether I could open the door' would focus more on my ability.
